title: Qualitative Characteristics
description: Understand relevance, faithful representation and other reporting qualities.
html:
What makes financial information useful?

Financial information is useful when it helps users make better economic decisions.

Two fundamental qualitative characteristics are especially important: relevance and faithful representation.

1. Relevance

Information is relevant when it can influence a user's decision.

Relevant information may have:

  • Predictive value
  • Confirmatory value
  • Materiality

Materiality Example

A $10 error may be insignificant for a company with billions of dollars in assets.

But a $10,000,000 error could clearly affect the decisions of investors and creditors.

2. Faithful Representation

Financial information should represent the economic substance of what actually occurred.

Faithful representation aims to be:

  • Complete
  • Neutral
  • Free from material error

Enhancing characteristics

Other characteristics can make useful information even better.

Characteristic
Meaning
Why It Matters
Comparability
Allows comparison
Helps compare companies or periods
Verifiability
Can be supported
Improves confidence in information
Timeliness
Available in time
Information can still affect decisions
Understandability
Clearly presented
Helps knowledgeable users interpret it

Big idea

Useful financial information should first be relevant and faithfully represented.

Comparability, verifiability, timeliness and understandability enhance that usefulness.

quiz.prompt: Which of the following is a fundamental qualitative characteristic of useful financial information?
quiz.explanation: Relevance and faithful representation are fundamental qualitative characteristics. Timeliness, comparability, verifiability and understandability are enhancing characteristics.
